reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes PlusToken as a cryptocurrency wallet and arbitrage service, directs viewers to download it, and links sending multiple currencies to stated daily profits of 6% to 18%. It also claims that entrusted assets are protected from price fluctuation while presenting the app as an income source, combining an asset transfer request with specific recurring returns and protection claims. Whether the download worked, returns were paid, or any transaction occurred is not established.

citations.quote: Today I am going to talk to you about the Plus Token Business App, a mobile application which generates revenue through the digital economy and its resulting business opportunity.

the so-called IE dog artificial intelligence is an arbitrage trading robot it identifies compares and uses the price differences and volumes of various crypto currencies on different trading platforms and carries out the arbitrage trade at the right moment.
You can send multiple currencies into the arbitrage trade.
The RE Dog will generate profits for you, which range between 6% and 18%, and are credited to your account daily.
The assets entrusted to us are completely unaffected by price fluctuation.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does give a concrete custody warning: users are told to keep their private keys safe, and the account is described as accessible only through the user's private key. The speaker also says users can pause the trading feature. Those statements do not verify the app's safety or returns, but they matter to how the video presents user control. The profits are described as a feature of the app, not accompanied by a request to disclose a private key. The more grounded reading is an explanation of a wallet and its trading feature that includes an operational warning, rather than an attempt to obtain viewers' credentials.

citations.quote: As a consequence, you should keep your private key SAFE
the user of the app manages its financial assets himself and it's only he who has access to his account which is through his private key
Of course, you can make your IEDog pause at any time.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited profit statement establishes what the speaker claims, not that any return was earned or that the wallet took control of an account. The description of sending currencies into arbitrage should be read alongside the speaker's specific warning to safeguard the private key. That context does not prove the service is trustworthy, but it complicates the claim that the video is simply asking viewers to surrender their assets.

citations.quote: The RE Dog will generate profits for you, which range between 6% and 18%, and are credited to your account daily.
As a consequence, you should keep your private key SAFE

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A private-key warning is not a warning that the advertised returns might fail. The video tells viewers they can send currencies into the arbitrage trade, says the robot will generate profits of 6% to 18% credited daily, and claims entrusted assets are unaffected by price fluctuation. User-control language does not qualify those financial promises or establish that the claimed protections work.

citations.quote: You can send multiple currencies into the arbitrage trade.
The RE Dog will generate profits for you, which range between 6% and 18%, and are credited to your account daily.
The assets entrusted to us are completely unaffected by price fluctuation.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the presentation explains what the app purports to do: it calls Plus Token both a digital-asset wallet and a trading platform, lists currencies it can store, and describes an arbitrage robot comparing prices and volumes across platforms. The return figure is a claim within that account of the product, not evidence in itself that a viewer invested or received anything. The video can be assessed as an explanation of a cryptocurrency tool without treating the speaker's unverified performance claim as an established outcome.

citations.quote: Plus Token is both a decentralised digital Assets Wallet and a trading platform for cryptocurrency's
one can store many different cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Thorarium, Litecoin, Ripple and others.
it identifies compares and uses the price differences and volumes of various crypto currencies on different trading platforms and carries out the arbitrage trade at the right moment.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies the stated return and the invitation to send currencies into arbitrage. Neither quote demonstrates a completed transfer, an actual payout, or how the robot performs. The same narration gives an account of the proposed trading operation; a judge should distinguish the speaker's description of a tool from independently established financial results.

citations.quote: You can send multiple currencies into the arbitrage trade.

the so-called IE dog artificial intelligence is an arbitrage trading robot it identifies compares and uses the price differences and volumes of various crypto currencies on different trading platforms

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Explaining a claimed mechanism does not make this a neutral technical lesson. The speaker presents the app as a business opportunity, tells viewers they can send currencies into the trade, and asserts daily credited profits. The concern is the video's promotion of those claims, not proof that a transfer or payout occurred.

citations.quote: a mobile application which generates revenue through the digital economy and its resulting business opportunity.
You can send multiple currencies into the arbitrage trade.
The RE Dog will generate profits for you, which range between 6% and 18%, and are credited to your account daily.

opening.argument: Judge, the observable offer is an app described as a wallet and cryptocurrency trading platform, with a description pointing viewers to a download. The supplied material does not show a completed deposit, a request for the viewer's password or private key, or anyone receiving a payout. Indeed, the speaker says the platform cannot access passwords or conduct transactions on the user's behalf. Those assurances should not be accepted as proof of safety, but neither should an unverified product pitch alone be treated as evidence that the service took a viewer's funds. This is a commercial presentation of a financial app whose claims warrant skepticism.

citations.quote: Plus Token is both a decentralised digital Assets Wallet and a trading platform for cryptocurrency's
Connecting to PlusToken is easy, download Wallet, wallet for IOS, (I-Phone): https://appdown.globalonline.cc/ios/share.htm ...
The Plus Token Platform itself has no access to your passwords and cannot conduct any transactions or anything like this.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Sending currencies into an arbitrage trade is described, but the opening does not identify a completed deposit or show where funds went. Nor does the stated daily credit establish an actual payout. The download instruction is consistent with an app promotion; the record leaves the service's real operation unresolved. The case should not rest on assuming outcomes the video does not show.

citations.quote: You can send multiple currencies into the arbitrage trade.
The RE Dog will generate profits for you, which range between 6% and 18%, and are credited to your account daily.
Connecting to PlusToken is easy, download Wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed deposit is not needed to identify what this video promotes. The pitch explicitly invites users to send multiple currencies into arbitrage, promises profits of 6% to 18% credited daily, and says entrusted assets are unaffected by price fluctuation. Calling it a wallet or app promotion does not remove the investment-return mechanism at the center of the offer.
